solves.reason: Self-regulation is an 'alternative' method. Text states 'no mandatory ethical qualifications' and 'no enforceable industry code of conduct'.
'toothless statements of aspiration' - not powerful. 'responsible use of powerful computers'. 'fear of being suspended or struck off'.
'blind trust is not how we govern'. 'no obligatory certification'. 'well-meaning generalities'.
③ informed contradicts the original 'blind' - the passage criticizes blind trust, so replacing with informed reverses the argument.
② trivial replaces serious - weakens the criticism about lack of consequences for 'serious' moral failings.
④ behind replaces ahead - reverses 'put the public ahead of profit' to putting public behind profit, contradicting the intended duty.
The passage opens with 'an _____ way' - only 'alternative' fits contextually as a method of accountability.
'without _____ for violating them' - consequences is the logical word; without it, charters are toothless.
'Tech is the _____' - exception. Other professions are regulated, tech is the exception.
suggested = proposed. Both mean 'put forward for consideration'.
violating = breaching. Both mean 'breaking/transgressing rules'.
explosion = surge. Both indicate rapid, large increase. decline and absence are antonyms.
mandatory (compulsory) ↔ voluntary (by choice). Other options relate to different semantic axes.
aspiration (desire/ambition) ↔ resignation (acceptance/giving up). ambition is a synonym, not antonym.
(A) hold a conference = organize/host. (B) hold to account = make responsible/answerable.
'Formal set of rules governing behavior of profession members' = code of conduct. The key word is 'conduct'.
profession → professionals. Need a plural noun referring to people, parallel with 'like doctors'.
fail → failings. 'Serious moral _____' needs a plural countable noun meaning deficiencies/shortcomings.
'anyone else in _____ ' - the phrase describes doctors/lawyers/bankers in 'unelected positions of social responsibility'.
'these charters are just _____' - toothless statements of aspiration. Describes the ineffective nature of voluntary charters.
